title: Sam Parr on money, sobriety, and what "enough" means after selling The Hustle
summary: Sam Parr talks with Ryan Holiday about setting a $20M goal at 24 and hitting it by 31, why he still wants more, and why success never feels like arriving. He also covers investing in the business machine, email newsletters as a business model, buy-it-for-life, and getting sober. Mostly mindset, with a few sharp business lessons.

principles.text: Set a concrete number goal, work backwards from it, and hit it.
principles.quote: what sum do I need to have that I could spend that if I wanted to and never run out of money for the rest of my life and I came up with that number roughly $20 million and so I said by 30 I want to post post tax have that invested

principles.text: Spend on a business machine that turns $1 into more than $1. Treat spend as investment.
principles.quote: if I have a machine that turns $1 into $150 I want to spend all of my money into that machine

principles.text: Build a machine whose output exceeds its input. Costs rising alongside revenue is fine.
principles.quote: there's an input and then you have to build a machine that has the output that's higher than the input and that's actually kind of easy to do or rather it's simple to do

principles.text: Monetize early, because you need money to keep making the thing and attention fades.
principles.quote: is your product good and they're like yeah I'm like do you want to keep doing it yeah yeah then [ __ ] Char money and make money so you can continue doing it

principles.text: Email newsletters are a great business: few people, huge reach, high revenue per send.
principles.quote: is the email newsletter potentially one of the greatest business models of all time

principles.text: Success never feels like arriving. Even top founders feel insecure, so you can be insecure and still succeed.
principles.quote: it's awesome that I can be insecure and good at my job and succeed
